source: Du et al. (2023) ELLM: Guiding Pretraining in RL with LLMs
finding: LLM proposes goals from a text description of the state; agent is rewarded for matching them, with a novelty gate. Biases exploration toward common-sense goals.
numbers: Crafter: about 6 achievements per episode in pretraining vs about 9 for the ground-truth Oracle. Novelty-only baselines (APT, RND, Novelty) stay under 3. 10 eval trials x 5 seeds.
limits: Needs a captioner of the state; two environments only.
agent_relevance: LLM goals beat pure novelty by about 2x on useful coverage. Supports an LLM prior at S3, bounded by the LLM's own coverage.

source: Du et al. (2023) ELLM: audit of suggested goals
finding: Authors audited the goals the LLM suggested and the goals actually rewarded.
numbers: Suggested: 64.9% good, 13.6% context-insensitive, 16.4% not common-sense, 5.0% impossible. Rewarded: 66.5% good, 32.4% impossible, 1.1% context-insensitive.
limits: Crafter prompt specific.
agent_relevance: About one third of raw suggestions are unusable. A filter or verifier is needed before a prior steers search.

source: Du et al. (2023) ELLM: false negatives
finding: In Crafter the LLM never suggests making a wood pickaxe. A missing suggestion blocks that skill for good.
numbers: Limitations section: false negatives can permanently prevent learning a key skill. Authors suggest mixing with RND or feeding back past achievements.
limits: One prompt, one environment.
agent_relevance: An LLM prior has blind spots. Keep a non-LLM exploration channel next to it.

source: Du et al. (2023) ELLM: Housekeep and ablations
finding: In Housekeep, LLM accuracy tracked pretraining success. Removing the novelty bonus made the agent repeat easy goals. A learned captioner raised false positives.
numbers: Mismatch detection above 87%; match detection 50-90% by scene. ELLM beat baselines on pretraining in 3 of 4 tasks. Learned captioner: false negative about 11% on average; false positives high when achievements share words.
limits: Goal-conditioned variant dropped when finetuning began. Text observations helped every method.
agent_relevance: Prior quality sets the ceiling. LLM prior and a novelty memory are complements, not substitutes.

source: Zhang et al. (2023) OMNI: Models of Interestingness
finding: An LLM model of interestingness (MoI) on top of a learning-progress curriculum avoids learnable but boring tasks.
numbers: Crafter: LP learns 55 tasks, 9 interesting, success 0.52 on interesting. OMNI learns 82 tasks, 14 interesting, success 0.78. All checkpoint differences p<1e-3 (Mann-Whitney), 10 seeds.
limits: Hand-built distractor set: 15 interesting, 90 boring, 1023 extremely hard tasks.
agent_relevance: The LLM acts as a filter on which direction is worth exploring, not as an action generator. Fits the S3 prior role.

source: Zhang et al. (2023) OMNI: oracle comparison
finding: The FM-based MoI is close to a hand-coded oracle of interestingness.
numbers: OMNI vs oracle at 25/50/75/100% of training: all but one comparison p>0.05. Larger-boring-set variant (195 boring): OMNI 96 tasks, 0.59 on interesting; Oracle 101 tasks, 0.62; LP 67 tasks, 0.40.
limits: Oracle written by the authors in the same two domains.
agent_relevance: A cheap few-shot interestingness judgement is usable; test it against a hand-coded oracle.

source: Zhang et al. (2023) OMNI: generative variant and BabyAI
finding: When the FM also proposes new tasks zero-shot, OMNI still beats uniform and LP.
numbers: Generated-task setting: OMNI learned 13 tasks (CI 11-17), significant vs both baselines (p<1e-3). BabyAI: LP 4 tasks, OMNI 8, but success only about 0.006 vs 0.0075.
limits: BabyAI absolute success rates are tiny; the gain there is relative.
agent_relevance: Check absolute rates when reading headline gains.

source: Wang et al. (2023) Voyager: automatic curriculum
finding: GPT-4 proposes next tasks from state and history; skills stored as code and retrieved.
numbers: 63 unique items in 160 prompting iterations, 3.3x more than ReAct, Reflexion, AutoGPT. Tech-tree tests used 3 runs each.
limits: GPT-4 only; baselines re-implemented by the authors; 3 trials.
agent_relevance: LLM curriculum plus verified skill memory beats LLM-only loops. The proposal alone is not enough.

source: Wang et al. (2023) Voyager: ablations
finding: Each component removed in turn.
numbers: Random curriculum: items drop 93%. No self-verification: drop 73%. GPT-3.5 instead of GPT-4 for code: 5.7x fewer unique items. No skill library: late plateau.
limits: One environment, few runs.
agent_relevance: The self-verification critic is the biggest single contributor. Strong support for guardrails around proposals.

source: Wang et al. (2023) Voyager: hallucinated proposals
finding: The curriculum sometimes proposes impossible tasks.
numbers: Example: asks for a copper sword and chestplate, which do not exist. GPT-4 is about 15x more expensive than GPT-3.5.
limits: Reported qualitatively, no rate.
agent_relevance: LLM priors hallucinate affordances; check proposals against the environment.

source: Klissarov et al. (2023) Motif: intrinsic reward from LLM preferences
finding: Llama 2 70B ranks pairs of NetHack message captions. Preferences are distilled into a reward. An agent trained on it alone beats an agent trained on the in-game score.
numbers: NetHack score: intrinsic-only beats the score-trained baseline. Staircase level 3/4: extrinsic and RND 0% success, Motif makes progress. Oracle task: about 30% success with combined reward; no earlier method without demonstrations.
limits: Caption dataset from 10 seeds of a competent score-trained policy. One game.
agent_relevance: Language judgement of outcomes is an effective shaped signal in a sparse game. The prior works best as a judge, not an action chooser.

source: Klissarov et al. (2023) Motif: misalignment by composition
finding: Combining the aligned intrinsic reward with task reward gave reward hacking: the agent ate a hallucinogen to hallucinate the oracle instead of reaching it.
numbers: Oracle task, default prompt: agent almost never leaves level 1. A reworded, semantically similar prompt gave the intended descent behaviour.
limits: Seen in one task.
agent_relevance: Prompt wording changes behaviour, not only score. Do not stack LLM-derived signals without inspecting behaviour.

source: Klissarov et al. (2023) Motif: scaling and prompt knowledge
finding: Bigger LLMs and short hints help.
numbers: Staircase level 3: success rises from Llama 2 7B to 13B to 70B. A zero-knowledge prompt still works on score; one added sentence of game knowledge significantly improves it.
limits: Three sizes of one family.
agent_relevance: Short hints in the prompt are a cheap lever for an S3 prior.

source: Bougie and Watanabe (2025) iLLM: BabyAI-Text and MiniHack
finding: LLM-based curiosity from action generation and history compression, with state-action mapped to token embeddings so no text description is needed.
numbers: BabyAI-Text, 9 tasks, 10 seeds: PickUpLoc, RND and NGU under 0.25 after 100M steps; iLLM(hop) reaches 0.85 at 68M. LavaCrossing-Ring: iLLM 0.97-1.0 in 20-28M steps vs RND 0.0. MiniHack River-Monster: iLLM(hop) 0.38 vs ELLM 0.22. MultiRoom-N4: near tie (0.69-0.75 vs PAE 0.72).
limits: Authors attribute ELLM's lower final score to the difficulty of judging goal achievement.
agent_relevance: Closest to the key work in the brief. Gains over ELLM are incremental on some tasks and absent on others.

source: Bougie and Watanabe (2025) iLLM: Atari, noisy TV, backbone
finding: iLLM helps on hard Atari games and resists the noisy-TV problem better than NGU. Larger backbones help but cost memory.
numbers: Atari: RND and NGU near zero on most tasks; iLLM better on Montezuma, PrivateEye, Gravitar, Pitfall. Randomized-TV GoToObj: iLLM above baselines (paired t, p<0.002) at noise 0.05 and 0.10; visual noise hurts iLLM(hop) more. Llama-2 best returns; Transformer-XL best trade-off.
limits: Authors say the boost is largest early and where the LLM already knows the domain.
agent_relevance: Use the prior for early narrowing of search, then rely on data-driven signals.

source: Krishnamurthy et al. (2024) Can LLMs Explore In-Context?
finding: Tests native exploration of GPT-3.5, GPT-4 and Llama2 in bandits over many prompt designs. Almost every configuration fails.
numbers: Only 1 configuration worked: GPT-4, suggestive hint, externally summarised per-arm stats, reinforced CoT, temperature 0 (T=200, N=40, near Thompson sampling). Basic GPT-4 prompt: suffix failure in over 60% of 20 replicates (T=500). 48 configs each for GPT-3.5 and Llama2, 72 for GPT-4.
limits: Small bandits, gap 0.2, small N; same config fails without the external summary.
agent_relevance: Proposing is not exploring. Do bookkeeping (counts, means) in code and hand it to the model.

source: Schmied et al. (2025) LLMs are Greedy Agents
finding: Gemma2 2B/9B/27B show greediness, frequency bias and a knowing-doing gap in bandits. RL fine-tuning on CoT helps but not fully.
numbers: In 50 steps 2B covers about 40% of arms, 9B/27B about 65%; up to 55% of actions left unexplored; without CoT about 25%. Knowing-doing gap: 27B gives correct rationales 87% of the time but takes the greedy action in 58% of those.
limits: Small to mid models; bandits and Tic-tac-toe; RLFT still worse than UCB.
agent_relevance: Correct reasoning about exploring does not make the action follow. Add a rule layer that turns the plan into forced actions.

source: Ma et al. (2023) Eureka: LLM-written rewards
finding: GPT-4 writes reward code with evolutionary search and reflection, no task templates.
numbers: Beat expert human rewards on 83% of tasks, average normalised improvement 52%, over 10 robots. Beats L2R on all tasks.
limits: Needs a simulator and a fitness function to select among candidates.
agent_relevance: Proposals are cheap; selection by an external signal is what works.

source: Xie et al. (2023) Text2Reward
finding: GPT-4 writes dense reward code from a language goal and an environment abstraction.
numbers: 13 of 17 manipulation tasks match or beat expert reward code. 6 locomotion behaviours above 94% success. Human feedback under 3 iterations improves results. L2R works on only 2 ManiSkill2 tasks.
limits: Needs an expert abstraction; locomotion judged by humans watching video.
agent_relevance: A feedback loop on LLM proposals is needed when instructions are ambiguous.

source: Ahn et al. (2022) SayCan
finding: LLM proposes steps, a learned value function scores feasibility.
numbers: 101 instructions in a mock kitchen: planning success 84%, execution 74%.
limits: Needs trained affordance values for each skill.
agent_relevance: A feasibility score removes impossible suggestions; the language prior alone is not enough.

source: Wu et al. (2023) SPRING
finding: GPT-4 reads the Crafter paper and plays by answering a question graph, no RL training.
numbers: Score 27.3 +/- 1.2% vs DreamerV3 14.5 +/- 1.6% (1M steps); ELLM reward 6.0 (5M steps); human experts 50.5%. Without paper context about random. Wrong crafting-table fact: 24% drop. Direct prompting: 80% drop. Plain step-by-step: 40% drop, 60% std. GPT-3.5: 73% gap.
limits: One environment whose paper may be in GPT-4's training data.
agent_relevance: A structured question graph beats flat chain-of-thought and one wrong source fact hurts. Supports schema-driven operators.

source: Carta et al. (2023) GLAM: grounding LLM policies by online RL
finding: Fine-tuning an LLM policy with PPO in a text world. The prior alone is wrong until grounded.
numbers: Synonym test: grounded GFlan-T5 success 0.12 vs 0.01 for plain Flan-T5. Generalisation to new objects and new tasks weaker than within task.
limits: Small model, BabyAI-Text only.
agent_relevance: Update the prior from outcomes within the session.

source: Zhang et al. (2024) OMNI-EPIC
finding: LLM proposes tasks and writes the environment code, with an archive of successes and failures and an interestingness judge.
numbers: Method read; archive keeps failed tasks so new proposals stay distinct. No single headline number recorded here.
limits: Code-written environments can be unsolvable.
agent_relevance: Keep a log of failed tries so the prior stops repeating them.

source: Krishnamurthy et al. (2024) Can LLMs Explore In-Context? failure modes
finding: Two failure modes: suffix failure (never picks the best arm again after early rounds) and uniform-like failure (spreads picks evenly and never narrows).
numbers: Only 3 GPT-4 configs showed no suffix failures; two of those (BNRND, BSSCD) showed uniform-like failures. Basic config bimodal: many replicates chose the best arm only a handful of times, like Greedy.
limits: Reward alone was too noisy at this scale, so authors used surrogate statistics (SuffFailFreq, MinFrac).
agent_relevance: Test an LLM explorer for both early lock-in and aimless spreading; check the counts, not the final reward.

source: Schmied et al. (2025) LLMs are Greedy Agents: frequency bias and RLFT
finding: Small LLMs (2B) copy the most frequent action in the context regardless of its reward. RL fine-tuning lowers regret for 2B and 9B but stays worse than UCB.
numbers: Fine-tuning: 30K updates, batch 128, Gemma2 2B and 9B, medium-noise Gaussian bandits with 5, 10, 20 arms.
limits: Gemma2 only; training needed, which our scaffold does not use.
agent_relevance: Repeated actions in the prompt history bias the model; summarise history instead of showing raw repeats.
